def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes:
## Definition

Fix an integer $d\ge2$. The **reference open simplex** is
$$\widehat S_d:=\{\widehat x\in\mathbb R^d:\widehat x_i>0\ (1\le i\le d),\ \sum_{i=1}^d\widehat x_i<1\},$$
with closure $\overline{\widehat S_d}=\operatorname{conv}\{0,e_1,\ldots,e_d\}$.

A **matching affine simplicial mesh** of a bounded polyhedral open set
$\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ is a finite set $\mathcal T$ of closed,
nondegenerate $d$-simplices such that their union is $\overline\Omega$,
their interiors are pairwise disjoint, $\Omega$ is the interior of their
union, and the intersection of two distinct cells is either empty or a
whole face of each. Thus no lower-dimensional crack is omitted from
$\Omega$ while its surrounding cells are retained. Every interior facet is
incident to exactly two cells and every boundary facet to one. The faces of
a cell are the convex hulls of its vertex subsets. A facet means a face of
dimension $d-1$.

For each cell $K\in\mathcal T$, an affine bijection
$$F_K:\overline{\widehat S_d}\to K,\qquad F_K(\widehat x)=b_K+A_K\widehat x,$$
with invertible $A_K\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ is a **reference map**.
Choose the vertex order so $\det A_K>0$; this is the orientation convention
used for Piola formulas. Write $h_K:=\operatorname{diam}(K)$ and let
$\rho_K$ be the radius of the largest Euclidean ball contained in $K$.
A family $\{\mathcal T_h\}_{h\in H}$ is **shape regular** if there is a
finite $\sigma$ such that $h_K/\rho_K\le\sigma$ for every
$h\in H$ and $K\in\mathcal T_h$. This universal condition is vacuous for
an empty family.
This definition uses radius; references using the diameter of the inscribed
ball differ by a factor of two.

An affine image of the reference square is a parallelogram. A general
quadrilateral requires a nonaffine map and is outside this affine definition;
curved-cell approximation is not included here.
def-oriented-simplicial-cell-chains:
## Definition

Let $\mathcal T$ be a matching simplicial mesh as in
[[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]]. Set $C_{-1}(\mathcal T;\mathbb Z)=0$.
For $0\le k\le d$, let
$C_k(\mathcal T;\mathbb Z)$ be the free abelian group generated by ordered
$k$-faces $[v_0,\ldots,v_k]$, with the orientation relation
$$[v_{\pi(0)},\ldots,v_{\pi(k)}]=\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)[v_0,\ldots,v_k]$$
for every permutation $\pi$. Define $\partial_0:C_0\to C_{-1}$ to be the
zero map. For $1\le k\le d$, define the **simplicial boundary**
homomorphism $\partial_k:C_k\to C_{k-1}$ on a generator by
$$\partial_k[v_0,\ldots,v_k]:=\sum_{j=0}^k(-1)^j [v_0,\ldots,\widehat v_j,\ldots,v_k].$$
This is the oriented incidence convention; no geometric
integration is part of the definition. The identity
$\partial_{k-1}\partial_k=0$ is proved directly from this alternating
formula in the following lemma.
lem-simplicial-boundary-squared-zero:
## Statement

For every $1\le k\le d$, the boundary maps of
[[def-oriented-simplicial-cell-chains]] satisfy
$$\partial_{k-1}\circ\partial_k=0.$$
def-broken-and-conforming-polynomial-spa:
## Definition

Let $\mathcal T$ be a matching affine simplicial mesh of $\Omega$ as defined
in [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]]. Fix $k\in\mathbb N_0$,
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, and an integer $q\ge1$. On each
cell let $\mathbb P_k(K;\mathbb K^q)$ denote the
restrictions to $K$ of $\mathbb K^q$-valued polynomials of total degree at
most $k$. The **broken polynomial space** is the finite product
$$V_h^{\mathrm{br}}:=\prod_{K\in\mathcal T}\mathbb P_k(K;\mathbb K^q),$$
viewed as functions defined almost everywhere cell by cell. For an interior
facet $F=K\cap K'$, the **jump** is the difference of the two polynomial
traces, with either fixed ordering of $K,K'$; its vanishing is independent of
that ordering. The **conforming polynomial space** is
$$V_h^{\mathrm{conf}}:=\{v\in V_h^{\mathrm{br}}:v|_{F,K}=v|_{F,K'}\text{ on every interior facet }F\}.$$
The **zero-boundary subspace** consists of those $v\in V_h^{\mathrm{conf}}$
whose polynomial trace is zero on every boundary facet. These are algebraic
definitions. The Sobolev inclusions and the zero-boundary closure conclusion
are proved separately in the corresponding local theorems on matching
piecewise polynomials and zero-boundary values. If $\mathcal T=\varnothing$,
then $\Omega=\varnothing$ by the mesh definition; the empty product is the
zero vector space consisting of the unique empty function, and the trace
conditions are vacuous.
def-reference-finite-element-and-unisolv:
## Definition

Let $d\ge1$, let $\widehat K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a nonempty bounded open
reference cell, let $q\ge1$ be an integer, and let
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. A **reference finite element** is a
triple $(\widehat K,\widehat P,\widehat\Sigma)$ where $\widehat P$ is an
$N$-dimensional subspace of $[C(\overline{\widehat K};\mathbb K)]^q$ for
$N\in\mathbb N_0$ and
$\widehat\Sigma=(\widehat\sigma_1,\ldots,\widehat\sigma_N)$ is a list of
linear functionals on $\widehat P$ for which
$$J_{\widehat\Sigma}:\widehat P\to\mathbb K^N,\qquad J_{\widehat\Sigma}(p):=(\widehat\sigma_1(p),\ldots,\widehat\sigma_N(p)),$$
is bijective. The functionals are the **degrees of freedom** and the triple
is **unisolvent**. Its **shape functions** are the unique dual basis
$\widehat\phi_1,\ldots,\widehat\phi_N\in\widehat P$ satisfying
$\widehat\sigma_i(\widehat\phi_j)=\delta_{ij}$.

If $X$ is a vector space of functions on $\widehat K$ containing
$\widehat P$ and each $\widehat\sigma_i$ has a well-defined bounded linear
extension to $X$, the associated **reference interpolation operator** is
$$\widehat I:X\to\widehat P,\qquad \widehat I v:=\sum_{i=1}^N\widehat\sigma_i(v)\widehat\phi_i.$$
The definition of a reference finite element does not assert that any
particular list of functionals is unisolvent or bounded on a given Sobolev
space; those are separate proof obligations. For $N=0$, $\widehat P=\{0\}$,
$\mathbb K^0=\{0\}$, the empty list gives the unique bijection between these
zero spaces, and the shape-function list is empty. The corresponding
interpolation formula is the empty sum, hence the zero map into $\{0\}$.
lem-unisolvent-dofs-define-reference-int:
## Statement

Let $(\widehat K,\widehat P,\widehat\Sigma)$ be a reference finite element
with $N=\dim\widehat P$, dual shape functions $\widehat\phi_i$, and bounded
extensions of its degrees of freedom to a function space $X$ containing
$\widehat P$. Then the operator
$$\widehat I v:=\sum_{i=1}^N\widehat\sigma_i(v)\widehat\phi_i$$
is the unique linear map $X\to\widehat P$ satisfying
$\widehat\sigma_i(\widehat I v)=\widehat\sigma_i(v)$ for every $i$, and
$\widehat I p=p$ for every $p\in\widehat P$.
lem-reference-polynomial-norm-equivalenc:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$,
$\widehat S_d$ be the reference simplex, let $\widehat P$ be a finite
dimensional $\mathbb K$-space of polynomial functions on it, let
$\widehat F$ be any facet, and let integer $m\ge0$. For $1\le p,q\le\infty$ there is a finite
constant $C$ such that
$$|v|_{W^{m,p}(\widehat S_d)}+\|v\|_{L^p(\widehat F)}\le C\|v\|_{L^q(\widehat S_d)}\qquad(v\in\widehat P).$$
For every pair of integers $0\le m\le\ell$, there is also a finite
constant $C$ such that
$$|v|_{W^{\ell,p}(\widehat S_d)} \le C|v|_{W^{m,q}(\widehat S_d)}\qquad(v\in\widehat P).$$
For finitely many facets, one constant works for all of them. In particular,
every linear degree-of-freedom functional on $\widehat P$ is bounded with
respect to the $L^q(\widehat S_d)$ norm.
lem-affine-pullback-weak-derivatives-and:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $F(\widehat x)=A\widehat x+b$ be an affine bijection from a bounded open
set $\widehat K\subset\mathbb R^d$ to $K$, where $A$ is invertible, and let
$1\le p\le\infty$. For every integer $r\ge0$ and scalar
$v\in W^{r,p}(K)$, the pullback $\widehat v:=v\circ F$ belongs to
$W^{r,p}(\widehat K)$. For $r\ge1$ its first weak derivatives satisfy
$$D_{\widehat x_j}\widehat v=\sum_{i=1}^d A_{ij}(D_{x_i}v)\circ F,$$
and higher derivatives are obtained by applying this constant-matrix rule
repeatedly. In particular, for each $0\le m\le r$,
$$|\widehat v|_{W^{m,p}(\widehat K)}\le C(d,m)\|A\|^m|\det A|^{-1/p}|v|_{W^{m,p}(K)},$$
where $|\det A|^{-1/p}:=1$ for $p=\infty$. The reverse estimate holds
with $A^{-1}$ and $|\det A|^{1/p}$ in place of $A$ and
$|\det A|^{-1/p}$.
lem-shape-regular-affine-simplex-scaling:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $F_K(\widehat x)=b_K+A_K\widehat x$ map the fixed reference simplex
$\widehat S_d$ bijectively to a cell $K$ of a shape-regular family, and let
$h_K$ be its diameter and $\rho_K$ its inradius. There are constants
$c,C>0$, depending only on $d$, the reference simplex, and the shape
regularity bound, such that
$$c h_K\le s_{\min}(A_K)\le \|A_K\|\le C h_K, \qquad c h_K^d\le\det A_K\le C h_K^d.$$
For each facet $F$, its affine surface Jacobian is comparable to
$h_K^{d-1}$, and its altitude from the opposite vertex is comparable to
$h_K$. Thus Sobolev scaling constants can be expressed using $h_K$ alone,
with constants uniform over the family.
lem-oriented-facet-cancellation-on-match:
## Statement

Orient every top-dimensional cell of a matching simplicial mesh by the
ambient orientation of $\mathbb R^d$, and orient each facet by the induced
boundary convention of [[def-oriented-simplicial-cell-chains]]. In the sum
of the oriented boundaries of all top-dimensional cells, every interior
facet occurs twice with opposite signs; every boundary facet occurs once.
lem-affine-simplex-gauss-green-formula:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $K$ be a nondegenerate affine $d$-simplex and let
$G\in C^1(\overline K;\mathbb R^d)$. If $n_{K,F}$ is the outward unit
normal on each facet $F$, then
$$\int_K\operatorname{div}G\,dx=\sum_{F\subset\partial K}\int_FG\cdot n_{K,F}\,dS.$$
For an orientation-preserving affine map $F_K(\widehat x)=b+A\widehat x$,
the oriented area element transforms as
$$n_{K,F}\,dS=\det(A)A^{-T}\widehat n_{\widehat F}\,d\widehat S.$$
lem-smooth-density-on-reference-simplex:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\ge2$, $k\in\mathbb N_0$,
$1\le p<\infty$, and let
$\widehat S_d$ be the reference simplex. Then restrictions of functions
smooth on a neighbourhood of $\overline{\widehat S_d}$ are dense in
$W^{k,p}(\widehat S_d)$ in its Sobolev norm. No density assertion for
$p=\infty$ is made.
thm-reference-simplex-sobolev-extension:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $d\ge2$. For every integer $k\ge0$ and
$1\le p\le\infty$, there is a bounded linear operator
$$E_{k,p}:W^{k,p}(\widehat S_d)\longrightarrow W^{k,p}(\mathbb R^d)$$
whose restriction to $\widehat S_d$ is the input class. Consequently
$\widehat S_d$ is a $W^{k,p}$-extension domain in the sense of
[[def-sobolev-extension-domain-and-extension-operator]]. The operator may
be chosen with support in one fixed bounded set.
thm-reference-simplex-trace-and-gauss-gr:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $1<p<\infty$ and $p'=p/(p-1)$. For each facet $F$ of
$\widehat S_d$, restriction of smooth functions extends uniquely to a
bounded linear trace map
$$\gamma_F:W^{1,p}(\widehat S_d;\mathbb R)\to L^p(F;\mathbb R).$$
For real-valued $u\in W^{1,p}(\widehat S_d)$ and
$G\in W^{1,p'}(\widehat S_d;\mathbb R^d)$, the facet traces satisfy
$$\int_{\widehat S_d}u\,\operatorname{div}G+\nabla u\cdot G\,dx =\sum_{F\subset\partial\widehat S_d}\int_F\gamma_Fu\,\gamma_FG\cdot\widehat n_F\,dS.$$
Here $\gamma_FG$ is the componentwise trace and $\widehat n_F$ is the
outward unit normal. The bounded C1-domain trace and Green theorems are not
used for the simplex.
thm-matching-continuous-piecewise-polyno:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\mathcal T$ be a finite matching affine simplicial mesh of a bounded
polyhedral open set $\Omega$, let $1\le p\le\infty$, and let $v$ be a
real-valued scalar member of the conforming piecewise-polynomial space in
[[def-broken-and-conforming-polynomial-spaces]]. Then $v\in W^{1,p}(\Omega)$.
Its weak gradient agrees almost everywhere on each cell with the ordinary
cellwise polynomial gradient.
thm-zero-boundary-piecewise-polynomials-:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega$ be a bounded polyhedral open set with a finite matching
affine simplicial mesh, let $1\le p<\infty$, and let $v$ be a real-valued
conforming piecewise polynomial whose polynomial trace vanishes on every boundary
facet. Then
$$v\in W^{1,p}_0(\Omega),\qquad \|v\|_{L^p(\Omega)}\le C_\Omega\|\nabla v\|_{L^p(\Omega)}.$$
Here $W^{1,p}_0$ is the norm closure of $C_c^\infty(\Omega)$; no C1
trace characterization is used.
thm-reference-simplex-poincare-wirtinger:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. For every $1\le p<\infty$ there is
$C_{d,p}<\infty$ such that for all
$u\in W^{1,p}(\widehat S_d;\mathbb R)$,
$$\|u-u_{\widehat S_d}\|_{L^p(\widehat S_d)} \le C_{d,p}|u|_{W^{1,p}(\widehat S_d)},\qquad u_{\widehat S_d}:=|\widehat S_d|^{-1}\int_{\widehat S_d}u\,dx.$$
thm-bramble-hilbert-on-reference-simplex:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $1\le p<\infty$, integer $r\ge1$,
integer $s\ge0$, and real-valued $v\in W^{\max(r,s),p}(\widehat S_d)$.
There is a polynomial $q\in\mathbb P_{r-1}(\widehat S_d)$, chosen by
matching all means $\int_{\widehat S_d}D^\alpha q=
\int_{\widehat S_d}D^\alpha v$ for $|\alpha|\le r-1$, such that:

- if $0\le s\le r$, then
  $\|v-q\|_{W^{s,p}(\widehat S_d)}\le C|v|_{W^{r,p}(\widehat S_d)}$;
- if $s>r$, then
  $\|v-q\|_{W^{s,p}(\widehat S_d)}\le
  C\sum_{j=r}^{s}|v|_{W^{j,p}(\widehat S_d)}$.

The second clause assumes $v\in W^{s,p}$; constants depend only on
$d,p,r,s$.
thm-local-finite-element-interpolation-e:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $k\ge0$, $1\le p<\infty$, and let
$(\widehat S_d,\widehat P,\widehat\Sigma)$ be a reference finite element
whose polynomial space contains $\mathbb P_k$. Assume its degrees of
freedom are bounded on $W^{\ell,p}(\widehat S_d)$ for an integer
$\ell\ge1$, let $r,m\in\mathbb N_0$, and let $\widehat I$ be its
interpolant. Thus
$\widehat Iq=q$ for $q\in\mathbb P_k$. On a shape-regular affine mesh
as in [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]], for each cell $K$ with its
orientation-preserving reference map $F_K$ define
$$I_Kv=(\widehat I(v\circ F_K))\circ F_K^{-1}.$$
For every such cell, if $\ell\le r\le k+1$ and $0\le m\le r$, then for
$v\in W^{r,p}(K)$,
$$|v-I_Kv|_{W^{m,p}(K)}\le C h_K^{r-m}|v|_{W^{r,p}(K)}.$$
If $\ell>k+1$ and $0\le m\le k+1$, then for $v\in W^{\ell,p}(K)$,
$$|v-I_Kv|_{W^{m,p}(K)} \le C\sum_{n=k+1}^{\ell}h_K^{n-m}|v|_{W^{n,p}(K)}.$$
The constants are uniform over the mesh family and depend on the stated
reference element, exponents and shape-regularity bound. For Lagrange
elements in the existing mesh dimension range $d\ge2$, assume additionally
the Axiom of Choice for the automatic nodal-boundedness application. Then
[[thm-lagrange-point-evaluation-threshold-on-reference-simplex]] supplies
the boundedness hypothesis when $\ell>d/p$; unisolvence of a particular
node set remains a separate hypothesis.
thm-polynomial-inverse-and-discrete-trac:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Fix polynomial degree $k\ge0$, $1\le p,q\le\infty$, and integers
$0\le m\le\ell\le k$. Let the shape-regular affine simplex family be as in
[[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]]. For every cell $K$ in that family,
there is a constant independent of cell size such that, for every
$v\in\mathbb P_k(K)$ and every facet $F\subset\partial K$,
$$|v|_{W^{\ell,p}(K)} \le C h_K^{m-\ell+d(1/p-1/q)}|v|_{W^{m,q}(K)},$$
$$\|v\|_{L^p(F)} \le C h_K^{(d-1)/p-d/q}\|v\|_{L^q(K)}.$$
Use $1/\infty=0$. Constants may depend on $d,k,p,q$ and the family shape
regularity bound, but not on $K$ or $h_K$.
def-covariant-contravariant-piola-maps-a:
## Definition

Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\ge2$, take $\widehat K=\widehat S_d$ as in
[[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]], and let $K=F(\widehat K)$ under an
affine cell map $F(\widehat x)=A\widehat x+b$ with $\det A>0$. Weak derivatives use the signed test identity of
[[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]. For $d\ge2$ define
$$H(\operatorname{div},K):=\{v\in L^2(K;\mathbb R^d):\operatorname{div}v\in L^2(K)\},$$
where $\operatorname{div}v=\sum_iD_i v_i$ weakly, meaning
$\int_Kv\cdot\nabla\phi=-\int_K(\operatorname{div}v)\phi$ for every
$\phi\in C_c^\infty(K)$. For $d=2$, define the weak scalar curl by
$\int_K(\operatorname{curl}v)\phi
=\int_K(v_1\partial_2\phi-v_2\partial_1\phi)$ for every
$\phi\in C_c^\infty(K)$. For $d=3$, define the weak vector curl by
$\int_K(\operatorname{curl}v)\cdot\psi
=\int_Kv\cdot\operatorname{curl}\psi$ for every
$\psi\in C_c^\infty(K;\mathbb R^3)$. In dimensions $d=2,3$ set
$$H(\operatorname{curl},K):=\{v\in L^2(K;\mathbb R^d):\operatorname{curl}v\in L^2(K;\mathbb R^{d_*})\},$$
with $d_*=1$ for $d=2$ and $d_*=3$ for $d=3$.

The **covariant Piola pushforward** of a reference vector field is
$$ (\mathcal P_F^{\mathrm{curl}}\widehat v)(F(\widehat x)):=A^{-T}\widehat v(\widehat x),$$
and the **contravariant Piola pushforward** is
$$ (\mathcal P_F^{\mathrm{div}}\widehat v)(F(\widehat x)):=\frac{1}{\det A}A\widehat v(\widehat x).$$
The scalar pullback is $u\mapsto u\circ F$. The exact mapping properties,
weak differential identities, and oriented trace-moment transformations
are established in the corresponding affine Piola theorem below.
thm-affine-piola-differential-and-trace-:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $d=2$ or $3$ and let $F(\widehat x)=A\widehat x+b$ map a reference
simplex to an affine cell with $\det A>0$. The contravariant Piola map
$\mathcal P_F^{\mathrm{div}}\widehat v=(\det A)^{-1}A\widehat v\circ F^{-1}$
maps $H(\operatorname{div},\widehat S_d)$ into $H(\operatorname{div},K)$ and
$$\operatorname{div}(\mathcal P_F^{\mathrm{div}}\widehat v) =(\det A)^{-1}(\widehat{\operatorname{div}}\widehat v)\circ F^{-1}.$$
The covariant Piola map
$\mathcal P_F^{\mathrm{curl}}\widehat v=A^{-T}\widehat v\circ F^{-1}$
maps $H(\operatorname{curl},\widehat S_d)$ into $H(\operatorname{curl},K)$;
in $d=2$ its scalar curl is
$(\det A)^{-1}(\widehat{\operatorname{curl}}\widehat v)\circ F^{-1}$,
and in $d=3$ its vector curl is
$(\det A)^{-1}A(\widehat{\operatorname{curl}}\widehat v)\circ F^{-1}$.
For smooth fields, contravariant normal fluxes satisfy
$v\cdot n\,dS=\widehat v\cdot\widehat n\,d\widehat S$; covariant tangential
pullbacks satisfy $v(F(\widehat x))\cdot A\widehat\tau=
\widehat v(\widehat x)\cdot\widehat\tau$ for every reference tangent
$\widehat\tau$. Thus edge line integrals and normal-flux moments are
preserved, and face tangential moments transform with this pullback and
the induced facet surface Jacobian. These formulas record the chosen
orientation; reversing a facet orientation reverses its signed moment.
lem-affine-piola-transport-preserves-com:
## Statement

Let $\widehat V_j$ and $V_j$ be reference and physical spaces related by
invertible affine Piola maps $P_j:\widehat V_j\to V_j$. Let $\widehat D_j$
and $D_j$ be the corresponding differential operators, and assume the
proved affine identities $D_jP_j=P_{j+1}\widehat D_j$ from
[[thm-affine-piola-differential-and-trace-moment-identities]]. Suppose
reference interpolation operators $\widehat I_j$ are defined on spaces
containing the relevant inputs and satisfy
$$\widehat D_j\widehat I_j=\widehat I_{j+1}\widehat D_j$$
there. Define the physical interpolants by Piola conjugation
$I_j=P_j\widehat I_jP_j^{-1}$. Then
$$D_jI_j=I_{j+1}D_j$$
on every input for which these compositions are defined. This is conditional
on the reference commuting identity; it does not assert that arbitrary
unisolvent degrees of freedom commute.
thm-lagrange-point-evaluation-threshold-:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $d\ge2$, let $N\in\mathbb N_0$, choose
$x_1,\ldots,x_N\in\overline{\widehat S_d}$, and let
$\ell\ge1$ be an integer. If $1\le p<\infty$ and $\ell>d/p$, then each
point evaluation has a unique continuous-representative value and
$$|u(x_j)|\le C\|u\|_{W^{\ell,p}(\widehat S_d)}.$$
If $p=\infty$, the same conclusion holds for every $\ell\ge1$.
Consequently any finite set of Lagrange nodal evaluations is bounded on
the stated Sobolev space and defines a well-defined degree-of-freedom
functional there. No boundedness at $\ell=d/p$ is asserted.
ex-affine-triangle-and-parallelogram-map:
## Statement

The orientation-preserving map $F(x,y)=(2x,3y)$ sends the reference
triangle $\widehat S_2=\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0),(1,0),(0,1)\}$ to the
triangle with vertices $(0,0),(2,0),(0,3)$ and area $3$. The affine map
$G(s,t)=(2s+t,3t)$ sends the unit square to the parallelogram with vertices
$(0,0),(2,0),(1,3),(3,3)$ and area $6$.
ex-shape-regular-and-sliver-triangle-fam:
## Statement

Uniform subdivisions of a fixed equilateral triangle into equilateral
cells of side $1/n$ form a shape-regular family with $h/\rho=2\sqrt3$.
For $\epsilon=1/n$, triangulate the fixed unit square into horizontal
strips of height $\epsilon$, each split along a diagonal. Its cells include
translates and reflections of the triangle with vertices
$(0,0),(1,0),(0,\epsilon)$; their $h/\rho\to\infty$, so this mesh family
is not shape regular under the convention of
[[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]].
cex-critical-lagrange-point-evaluation-o:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. For any interior point $c$ of the reference triangle, point evaluation
$u\mapsto u(c)$ is not bounded on smooth functions equipped with the
$W^{1,2}(\widehat S_2)$ norm. Thus the critical case $\ell=d/p=1$ cannot
be added to the supercritical point-evaluation conclusion.
ex-oriented-boundary-cancellation-on-two:
## Statement

Split the unit square along the diagonal from $v_0=(0,0)$ to
$v_2=(1,1)$, with $v_1=(1,0)$ and $v_3=(0,1)$. Orient the two triangles
counterclockwise as $[v_0,v_1,v_2]$ and $[v_0,v_2,v_3]$. Their shared
diagonal occurs once with each orientation and cancels in the sum of their
oriented boundaries.
